title: SDK: streaming reconnect + typed streaming/network errors (templates readiness)
author: Dana Lo
body:
Context: The Quickstart Templates (RAG + agents) rely heavily on streaming. In internal beta we saw a few recurring failure modes: (1) intermittent disconnects mid-stream behind certain proxies (SUP-29410), (2) ambiguous errors from the TS SDK (callers can’t reliably distinguish user abort vs network reset vs server error), (3) retry loops that accidentally duplicate output when users implement naive reconnect.

This PR improves streaming resilience in the TypeScript SDK and introduces a more precise error taxonomy so templates (and end users) can implement safe defaults: bounded retries, correct user messaging, and better observability tags.

What changed (high-level):
- Add opt-in streaming reconnect for SSE/streaming chat completions, with guardrails to prevent unbounded loops and to minimize duplicate output.
- Introduce first-class error types for network/stream/auth/rate-limit/timeout scenarios, including structured fields (status, requestId, retryAfterMs, isRetryable).
- Normalize abort handling: explicit AbortError mapping and consistent behavior when AbortSignal is triggered.
- Improve parsing/handling of partial SSE frames so transient chunk corruption doesn’t crash the whole stream.

API changes:
- New error classes exported from the SDK: RedwoodError (base), RedwoodAPIError, RedwoodAuthError, RedwoodRateLimitError, RedwoodQuotaError, RedwoodNetworkError, RedwoodTimeoutError, RedwoodStreamError, RedwoodAbortError.
- Reconnect support is exposed via a new option on streaming requests: streamReconnect: { enabled: boolean; maxRetries?: number; initialBackoffMs?: number; maxBackoffMs?: number; jitter?: boolean; retryOn?: (err) => boolean }.
- Default remains NO reconnect (enabled=false). Templates will enable it with conservative defaults.

Breaking change notes:
- Errors thrown by the SDK are now instances of the new Redwood*Error classes in more cases where we previously threw generic Error with message text. If callers were matching on error.message substrings, they should migrate to instanceof checks or error.type.
- The previous exported type guard isRedwoodErrorResponse() has been removed in favor of typed errors (see MIGRATION.md in this PR). If you used it, replace with `err instanceof RedwoodAPIError` and inspect `err.status`/`err.code`.

Reconnect behavior details:
- Only retries on errors that are likely transient (network reset, gateway 502/503/504, EOF during SSE) and only if we have not emitted any tokens OR if the caller enables `allowPartialReplay` (defaults false). This is to avoid duplicating output.
- When reconnecting, we create a fresh request and annotate it with `x-redwood-retry-attempt` for supportability; request IDs are still captured per attempt.
- Max retries default is 2 when enabled; backoff defaults: 250ms -> 1s (with jitter).

Implementation notes:
- Streaming is implemented on top of fetch + ReadableStream; we now wrap the body reader with a small state machine that tolerates partial lines and emits StreamEvent objects.
- We attach `requestId` from response headers (when available) to all RedwoodAPIError/RedwoodStreamError instances.
- We thread a stable `clientRequestId` through retries for logs/traces correlation.

Testing:
- Added unit tests for error mapping (status-based and fetch-level errors).
- Added deterministic tests for reconnect backoff using fake timers.
- Added a smoke test that simulates an SSE stream that disconnects after N events and verifies retry stops at maxRetries.

Rollout:
- This will ship in the next minor (0.31.0). Templates will pin to >=0.31.0 once released.

Docs:
- Added MIGRATION notes and updated README snippets to demonstrate `instanceof RedwoodRateLimitError` and recommended backoff handling.

Checklist:
- [x] Matches template safe-defaults policy (bounded retries, no token replay by default)
- [x] Captures and exposes x-request-id/request-id on errors
- [x] No high-cardinality fields added to default logs (requestId only)
- [x] CI green

Refs:
- Linear: ENG-4183 (TS template), ENG-4186 (streaming smoke tests), ENG-4189 (request id propagation)
- Support: SUP-29410 (streaming disconnects behind proxies)
commits: sdk(ts): add Redwood*Error hierarchy + error mapping helpers
sdk(ts): implement optional streaming reconnect with bounded retries + backoff
sdk(ts): harden SSE parser for partial frames and unexpected EOF
tests(ts): add reconnect and abort behavior tests (fake timers)
docs: add MIGRATION notes + update streaming examples
changed_files: src/http/response.ts: normalize request-id extraction and header parsing
src/http/fetcher.ts: map fetch/timeout/abort into typed errors
src/streaming/sse.ts: tolerant SSE parser + event iterator
src/client.ts: expose streamReconnect option on streaming methods
test/errors.spec.ts: status + network error mapping coverage
MIGRATION.md (new): guidance for upgrading error handling
conversation: Ibrahim Khan (review): We should be extremely careful about output duplication. I like the default of not replaying partial streams. Can we also ensure we never retry after emitting any content unless the caller explicitly opts in?
Dana Lo (author): Yep—implemented as `hasEmittedTokens` guard. By default we only retry if nothing has been emitted. I added a comment + unit test for the partial emission case.
Brian Murphy (review): For request-id: are we extracting from both `x-request-id` and `x-redwood-request-id`? Gateway behavior varies across deployments.
Dana Lo (author): Added fallback order: x-redwood-request-id -> x-request-id -> request-id. Also exposed as `err.requestId` for all RedwoodAPIError and RedwoodStreamError.
Christine Wong (review): Backoff defaults look okay, but I want max elapsed time to be bounded too. Otherwise maxRetries=10 could mean a long hang. Can we cap overall retry window?
Dana Lo (author): Good catch. Added `maxTotalRetryMs` (default 8000ms when enabled). The retry loop stops when exceeded even if retries remain. Updated tests.
Sahana Iyer (CI/build): The streaming smoke test flaked once due to timers; can we avoid real setTimeout in tests?
Dana Lo (author): Switched to fake timers for backoff and used a deterministic stream stub. Reran CI twice; stable.
Ibrahim Khan (approval): Approved with the guardrails + maxTotalRetryMs. Please ensure templates enable reconnect explicitly (no SDK default).
Dana Lo (author): Confirmed—SDK default remains disabled. Templates will set enabled=true with maxRetries=2 and maxTotalRetryMs=8000ms.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Dana Lo after approvals; release branch to be cut as part of 0.31.0.
release_notes: TypeScript SDK: Added typed Redwood*Error classes for more reliable error handling (rate limits, auth, network, streaming).
TypeScript SDK: Optional streaming reconnect with bounded retries/backoff for improved resilience behind flaky networks/proxies (disabled by default).
Migration: If you previously matched on error.message substrings or used isRedwoodErrorResponse(), migrate to instanceof checks and inspect err.status/err.requestId.
